issues.description: Field de.tum.cit.ase.Farm.animals: The UML in the problem statement declares the animals attribute as private ("- animals: List<Animal>") and the instructions ask students to provide a getter and a setter. The solution implementation declares the field as public (public List<Animal> animals; in the solution Farm.java), while the template Farm.java currently contains only a TODO and no field. This mismatch between the UML/instructions (private field + getter/setter) and the solution (public field) breaks the encapsulation intended by the exercise and may confuse students about whether they should access the list directly or via the getter/setter.
issues.suggestedFix: Declare the animals field as private in the implementation: private List<Animal> animals; Keep or provide public getter and setter methods (getAnimals(), setAnimals(List<Animal>)). Update any internal code in Farm (and other classes if any) to use the getter/setter rather than direct field access (e.g., use getAnimals().add(animal) in addAnimal, iterate getAnimals() in feedAllAnimals and singFarmSong). This preserves the encapsulation shown in the UML and aligns the implementation with the exercise instructions.
